explanation: Reproduction is the biological process by which existing parent organisms produce new offspring of their own kind.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: What mode of plant reproduction produces new plants WITHOUT the involvement or production of seeds?
explanation: Asexual reproduction (including vegetative propagation, budding, fragmentation, spore formation) generates new plants without seeds.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: What are the vegetative parts of a plant that can produce new plants in Vegetative Propagation?
explanation: Vegetative propagation utilizes non-floral somatic organs: roots, modified stems, and foliar leaves.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: What are the small vegetative scars/notches on a Potato tuber that contain buds capable of growing into new potato plants called?
explanation: Potato tubers are modified underground storage stems with nodal 'eyes' containing vegetative axillary buds.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: Which plant reproduces vegetatively by producing adventitious vegetative buds along the margins of its thick fleshy LEAVES?
explanation: Bryophyllum reproduces foliar vegetatively: marginal leaf notches develop adventitious plantlets that root upon falling onto moist soil.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: What is the primary reproductive organ of a flowering plant for Sexual Reproduction?
explanation: Flowers are specialized angiosperm reproductive shoots bearing male (stamens) and female (carpels/pistils) organs.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: What is the MALE reproductive organ of a flower called, consisting of an Anther and Filament?
explanation: The stamen is the male floral organ comprising a filament supporting a terminal anther that synthesizes pollen grains.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: What is the FEMALE reproductive organ of a flower called, consisting of Stigma, Style, and Ovary?
explanation: The pistil/carpel consists of a receptive stigma, slender style, and a basal ovary enclosing ovules with egg cells.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: Flowers that contain EITHER only stamens (male) OR only pistils (female) — like Papaya, Corn, and Cucumber — are called:
explanation: Unisexual (imperfect) flowers possess either androecium or gynoecium exclusively (e.g. dioecious papaya, monoecious maize).

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: Flowers that contain BOTH stamens and pistil within the same flower — like Mustard, Rose, and Petunia — are called:
explanation: Bisexual (hermaphroditic/perfect) flowers bear functional stamens and carpels in the same floral whorl.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower is called:
explanation: Pollination is the mechanical transference of pollen grains from anther to receptive stigma by wind, water, or biotic vectors.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: The process of fusion of the male gamete with the female gamete (egg cell) to form a single-celled ZYGOTE is called:
explanation: Fertilization (syngamy) is the fusion of haploid male and female gametic nuclei inside the embryo sac to form a diploid zygote.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: How does single-celled Yeast reproduce asexually under favorable nutrient conditions?
options: By BUDDING: a small bulb-like projection (bud) gradually grows from the parent cell, receives a replicated nucleus, and detaches to form a new yeast cell
explanation: Yeast multiplies rapidly via asymmetric mitotic budding: blastospores pinch off or form pseudo-mycelial chains.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: How do green filamentous Algae (like Spirogyra) multiplying rapidly in stagnant ponds reproduce asexually?
options: By FRAGMENTATION: the long green filament breaks into two or more fragments, and each fragment grows into a complete new individual
explanation: Spirogyra undergoes vegetative fragmentation: mechanical cleavage of multicellular filaments yields independent surviving clones.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: How do Fungi (like Bread Mold / Rhizopus), Mosses, and Ferns reproduce asexually?
options: By SPORE FORMATION: microscopic spores protected by a hard, thick protective coat inside Sporangia disperse in air and germinate in moist conditions
explanation: Sporogenesis: sporangiophores bear resistant haploid sporangiospores capable of withstanding environmental desiccation.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: What is the difference between SELF-POLLINATION and CROSS-POLLINATION?
options: Self-pollination occurs when pollen lands on the stigma of the SAME flower or another flower on the SAME plant ; Cross-pollination occurs when pollen lands on a flower of a DIFFERENT plant of the same kind
Self-pollination is done by birds only
explanation: Self-pollination (autogamy/geitonogamy) transfers pollen within the same genetic individual; cross-pollination (xenogamy) transfers pollen between distinct plants.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: After successful fertilization in a flower, what do the OVARY and the OVULE develop into?
options: The OVARY ripens into the FRUIT ; and the OVULES develop into SEEDS containing the embryo
The ovary becomes a leaf and ovule becomes a flower
The ovary becomes root and ovule becomes stem
explanation: Post-fertilization morphogenesis: pericarp ovary wall develops into fruit; fertilized integumented ovules mature into seeds.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: Which of the following plants reproduces vegetatively through modified underground STEM RHIZOMES containing nodes and scaly buds?
explanation: Ginger (Zingiber) and Turmeric (Curcuma) propagate vegetatively via horizontal subterranean rhizomes bearing dormant axillary buds.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: Which plants reproduce vegetatively through fleshy swollen ROOT TUBERS?
explanation: Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) and Dahlia develop adventitious root tubers that sprout vegetative shoots.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: Why are light, winged seeds (such as Drumstick and Maple) and hairy parachutes (such as Aak / Madar and Dandelion) dispersed by WIND?
options: Their lightweight wings and tufts of fine hair act like aerodynamic sails and parachutes, allowing air currents to carry them far away
explanation: Anemochory adaptations: aerodynamic samara wings (Acer, Moringa) and pappus hair tufts (Calotropis, Taraxacum) facilitate wind buoyancy.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: How are fibrous, buoyant fruits like the Coconut (Cocos nucifera) dispersed across distant islands?
options: By WATER: the thick, spongy, fibrous mesocarp traps air, making coconuts float effortlessly across ocean waves for thousands of miles
By wind blowing them in clouds
explanation: Hydrochory adaptation: fibrous air-trapping coir mesocarp and impervious endocarp allow coconuts to float across marine currents.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: How are spiny seeds equipped with sharp hooks (such as Xanthium and Urena) dispersed to new habitats?
options: By ANIMALS: their hooked spines cling stubbornly to the fur of passing animals or human clothing and get transported far away
explanation: Epizoochory adaptation: stiff hooked spines on Xanthium burs latch onto animal pelts and fleece for long-distance transport.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: How do Castor and Balsam plants disperse their seeds through sudden explosive mechanical action?
options: Their ripe seed pods burst open suddenly with explosive jerks upon drying, flinging the seeds forcefully far away from the parent plant
explanation: Autochory / Ballochory: desiccation creates hygroscopic tissue tension that ruptures the capsule explosively, projecting seeds meters away.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: What is the horticultural advantage of Vegetative Propagation (like stem cuttings in Roses, Sugarcane, and Grapes) for farmers?
options: Plants grown vegetatively take much less time to bear flowers and fruits, and are exact genetic clones preserving all desirable parental qualities
They produce seeds with random changes
They do not need water or soil
explanation: Vegetative cloning bypasses juvenile seed dormancy, accelerates fruiting, and guarantees 100% true-to-type genetic fidelity.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: What grows out of a pollen grain after it lands on the sticky receptive stigma of a compatible flower?
options: A long Pollen Tube that grows downwards through the style to deliver male gametes into the ovary's ovule
explanation: Chemotropic pollen tube germination: the tube cell elongates through stylar transmitting tissue, conveying sperm nuclei to the micropyle.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: Why do insect-pollinated flowers (like Rose, Jasmine, and Sunflower) possess brightly colored petals, sweet fragrance, and sugary nectar?
options: To attract insect pollinators (bees, butterflies) which brush against anthers and carry sticky pollen grains to other flowers
To cool the flower during hot days
explanation: Entomophilous floral syndrome: chromatic showy corollas, volatile terpenes, and nectar rewards co-evolved to attract insect pollinators.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: What are the distinguishing characteristics of Wind-Pollinated flowers (like Grasses, Corn, and Wheat)?
options: They have small, dull non-scented flowers, enormous quantities of light dry powdery pollen, and large feathery stigmas exposed to catch windborne pollen
They have giant sweet-smelling red petals
explanation: Anemophilous floral syndrome: reduced perianth, non-sticky aerodynamically buoyant pollen produced in billions, and plumose stigmas.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Reproduction in Plants
question: Why is Seed Dispersal essential for the healthy survival and distribution of plant species?
options: It prevents intense competition for sunlight, water, minerals, and space among seedlings near the parent plant, while invading new geographic habitats
It keeps all seeds in one single spot
explanation: Seed dispersal reduces density-dependent sibling competition, mitigates pathogen transmission, and colonizes novel ecological niches.

question:

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: Amphimixis (sexual syngamy) generates novel allelic combinations via meiosis and cross-fertilization, fueling evolutionary fitness.

The style closes with a physical gate

question: Why do Spores produced by Fungi (Bread Mold) and Mosses survive extreme harsh conditions (heat, freezing cold, lack of moisture) for years?

Spores are made of pure stone
Spores are protected by adult animals

Flowers turning into seeds without petals

Cut down all flowers in winter

They protect the seed from birds only
explanation: Cotyledons (seed leaves) store nutritive endospermic reserves mobilized by amylases to fuel early heterotrophic seedling growth.

That flowers exist only for decoration
That all plants will stop reproducing in the future

options: A narrow strip of land in West Bengal (~22 km wide at its narrowest) connecting the entire eight states of Northeast India with the rest of mainland India
A bridge between India and Sri Lanka
A canal through the Thar desert
explanation: The Siliguri Corridor is the critical geopolitical chokepoint linking mainland India to the eight northeastern sister states.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 8: Indian Geography, Physical Features, Climate & Resources
question: Why is the Chota Nagpur Plateau in eastern India celebrated as the 'Ruhr of India'?
options: It contains the richest concentration of metallic and mineral wealth in India, including massive reserves of Iron Ore, Coal (Jharia, Bokaro), Mica, Bauxite, and Uranium
Because it has the most rivers
Because it is covered in snow all year
explanation: Like Germany's Ruhr basin, the Chota Nagpur plateau is India's mineral heartland, powering the nation's steel and heavy manufacturing.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 8: Indian Geography, Physical Features, Climate & Resources
question:
Consider four major multi-purpose river valley projects in India:
1. Bhakra Nangal Dam (Satluj River - Punjab/Himachal)
2. Tehri Dam (Bhagirathi River - Uttarakhand, highest dam in India)
3. Hirakud Dam (Mahanadi River - Odisha, longest earthen dam)
4. Sardar Sarovar Dam (Narmada River - Gujarat)
What primary developmental benefits do these dams provide?
options: Hydroelectric power generation, extensive canal irrigation networks for agriculture, flood mitigation, and industrial drinking water security
They stop all rivers from flowing
They are built only for boating tourist sports
They turn fresh water into salt water
explanation: Multi-purpose hydro projects (Nehru's 'Temples of Modern India') integrate hydroelectric generation, perennial irrigation, and flood mitigation.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 8: Indian Geography, Physical Features, Climate & Resources
question: What is the 'Tropical Evergreen Forest' biome in India (found in the Western Ghats, Northeast India, and Andaman & Nicobar)?
options: Dense, multi-layered rain forests receiving >200 cm rainfall with trees (Rosewood, Mahogany, Ebony) that do not shed leaves simultaneously, remaining green throughout the year
Forests with thorny bushes and no leaves
Forests that only grow in snow
explanation: Tropical evergreen rainforests exhibit complex vertical stratification, dense multi-tiered canopies, and immense biodiversity.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 8: Indian Geography, Physical Features, Climate & Resources
question: What is the 'Indira Point' in the Nicobar Islands?
options: The southernmost geographic point of the sovereign territory of the Republic of India (located at 6° 45' N on Great Nicobar Island)
The easternmost point in Arunachal Pradesh
explanation: Indira Point on Great Nicobar (submerged partially in the 2004 tsunami) marks India's southernmost geographical point.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 8: Indian Geography, Physical Features, Climate & Resources
question: Why is the Western Ghats recognized by UNESCO as one of the world's eight 'Hottest Hotspots' of Biological Diversity?
options: It harbors thousands of endemic species of flora, fauna, birds, amphibians, and reptiles found nowhere else on Earth, amidst high anthropogenic habitat pressure
Because it is the hottest desert on Earth
Because it has active gold mines
explanation: The Western Ghats harbor immense floral/faunal endemism (Lion-tailed macaque, Nilgiri tahr, Malabar gliders) under acute conservation vulnerability.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 8: Indian Geography, Physical Features, Climate & Resources
question: What overarching geographic reality defines the Indian Subcontinent in Chapter 8 of General Knowledge?
options: An extraordinary physical mosaic uniting towering Himalayan snow ranges, fertile riverine alluvial plains, ancient mineral-rich plateaus, sun-drenched coastlines, and monsoon rhythms that sustain India's immense biological and civilizational vitality
A uniform desert with no physical variation
An island completely cut off from the rest of the world
A land without any rivers or forests
explanation: Chapter 8 synthesizes India's diverse physiography, drainage basins, tropical monsoon meteorology, and precious mineral-ecological patrimony.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: In medieval South India (7th to 9th centuries), who were the poet-saints who led the vibrant Bhakti movement devoted to LORD SHIVA?
options: The Nayanars (63 Nayanars including Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar)
explanation: The Nayanars were 63 Shaivite Bhakti saints belonging to diverse caste backgrounds (potters, untouchables, peasants, kings).

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Who were the South Indian Bhakti poet-saints who immersed themselves in passionate devotion to LORD VISHNU?
options: The Alvars (12 Alvars including Periyalvar, Andal, Nammalvar)
explanation: The 12 Alvars were Vaishnavite mystic saints whose devotional Tamil songs were compiled in the sacred Divya Prabandham.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Who was the only celebrated WOMAN Alvar saint among the twelve Alvars, known for her deeply emotional devotional poetry to Lord Krishna (Ranganatha)?
explanation: Andal (daughter of Periyalvar) is the revered female Alvar saint who composed the Thiruppavai in ecstatic devotion to Lord Vishnu.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Which 12th-century socio-religious movement in Karnataka was initiated by Basavanna, Allama Prabhu, and Akkamahadevi, advocating equality of all humans and rejecting caste discrimination and idol worship?
explanation: Basavanna and his companions founded the Virashaiva movement, rejecting ritual orthodoxy, caste hierarchies, and the mistreatment of women.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Which local temple deity at Pandharpur in Maharashtra became the supreme focus of the Varkari Bhakti tradition led by Jnaneshwar, Namdev, Eknath, and Tukaram?
options: Lord Vitthala (a manifestation of Lord Vishnu / Krishna)
explanation: The Varkari sect centered on the worship of Lord Vitthala (Vithoba) in the grand temple at Pandharpur on the Bhima river.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Who was the 15th-century mystic weaver-poet of Varanasi who expressed his passionate devotion to formless God (Nirguna Bhakti) through rhyming couplets called Sakhis and Pads?
explanation: Sant Kabir preached formless monotheism, fiercely mocking external religious rituals, hypocrisy, and caste prejudices in Hinduism and Islam.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Who was the founder of SIKHISM, born at Talwandi (Nankana Sahib in Pakistan) in 1469, who emphasized devotion to One Formless Creator (Ik Onkar) and set up the Langar community kitchen?
explanation: Guru Nanak Dev Ji founded Sikhism, established the sacred congregation (Dharamsal/Sangat), and instituted the egalitarian community kitchen (Langar).

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Who was the 5th Sikh Guru who compiled the holy hymns of Guru Nanak and other Bhakti and Sufi saints (Kabir, Baba Farid, Namdev) into the Adi Granth in 1604?
explanation: Guru Arjan Dev Ji compiled the Adi Granth in 1604 at Amritsar, which was later consecrated as the eternal Guru Granth Sahib by Guru Gobind Singh in 1708.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Who was the Rajput princess of Mewar who rejected royal luxury and became an ardent, fearless disciple of the saint Ravidas, composing passionate devotional Bhajans to Lord Krishna (Giridhar Gopal)?
explanation: Mirabai defied royal patriarchal conventions, dedicating her life to pure Saguna Krishna devotion and egalitarian saintly fellowship.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Who composed the monumental epic 'Ramcharitmanas' in the Awadhi dialect of Hindi, portraying Lord Rama as the supreme embodiment of compassion and devotion?
explanation: Sant Tulsidas authored the beloved Ramcharitmanas in vernacular Awadhi, making Rama's life accessible to millions across North India.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Which revered Sufi saint of the Chishti order made AJMER in Rajasthan his spiritual hospice, drawing millions of pilgrims to his sacred Dargah?
explanation: Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti (1142–1236) established the Chishti silsila in Ajmer, preaching universal love, tolerance, and service to the destitute.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Which 15th-century saint-reformer introduced the 'Ekasarana Dharma' (devotion to One Supreme Lord Krishna) in Assam, pioneering devotional music (Borgeet) and community prayer halls (Namghars)?
explanation: Srimanta Sankaradeva founded the Neo-Vaishnavite movement in Assam, establishing Satras and village Namghars (prayer houses).

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: What was Shankara's philosophical doctrine of 'ADVAITA' (Non-dualism) propounded in the 8th century in Kerala?
options: The fundamental oneness and identity of the individual soul (Atman) with the ultimate Supreme Reality (Brahman) ; the world is Maya (illusion) and true liberation comes through knowledge (Jnana)
That there are thousands of separate supreme gods
That the world is made of pure gold
That humans can never attain salvation
explanation: Adi Shankaracharya preached Advaita: absolute non-dual monism where Brahman alone is real, the empirical world is Maya, and Atman is Brahman.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: What was Ramanuja's 11th-century philosophical doctrine of 'VISHISHTADVAITA' (Qualified Non-dualism) preached in Tamil Nadu?
options: The individual soul remains distinct and qualified even when united with the Supreme Brahman through passionate, loving devotion (Bhakti) to Vishnu
That God has no love for humans
That all rituals must be conducted in silence
That souls are completely destroyed after death
explanation: Ramanuja harmonized Vedanta with Bhakti: the individual soul is an organic part (amsha) of Vishnu, finding salvation through loving surrender (Prapatti).

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: What are the famous canonical song anthologies of the Nayanars and the Alvars called in Tamil literature?
explanation: Nayanar hymns are compiled in the 12 Tirumurais (including Tevaram & Tiruvacakam); Alvar hymns comprise the 4,000 verses of the Divya Prabandham.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: What radical social reform did the Virashaiva Vachana literature champion in 12th-century medieval society?
options: Fierce denunciation of caste hierarchies, untouchability, sacrificial animal slaughter, and ritual pollution, while asserting the spiritual equality and independence of women
Forcing people to fast every day
explanation: Virashaiva Vachanas (by Basavanna, Allama, Akkamahadevi) attacked caste oppression, empty ritualism, and patriarchal subordination of women.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Why did the medieval Bhakti saints of Maharashtra (Jnaneshwar, Eknath, Tukaram) REJECT the traditional concept of ascetic renunciation (Sannyasa)?
options: They believed true spirituality lay in living as ordinary householders, earning an honest livelihood, and serving fellow human beings in distress with compassion (active social service)
Because they wanted to become wealthy kings
explanation: The Marathi saints humanized Bhakti: Tukaram proclaimed that he who recognizes the suffering of the distressed as his own is a true saint.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: What were the 'Khanqahs' of the Sufi masters in medieval India?
options: Hospices and community centers where Sufi Pir masters taught disciples, hosted spiritual assemblies (Sama), and fed travelers, nobles, and commoners from all walks of life
explanation: Khanqahs served as inclusive spiritual hospices where people of all faiths gathered for discourse, music, blessings, and community meals.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: What is 'Zikr' and 'Sama' in the devotional spiritual practice of Sufi mysticism?
options: Zikr is the rhythmic chanting/repetition of the divine Name of God ; Sama is spiritual music and audition evoking divine ecstatic love
Zikr is sword fighting and Sama is swimming
Zikr is eating food and Sama is sleeping
Both are names of desert horses
explanation: Sufi praxis: Zikr (contemplative remembrance of God) and Sama (ecstatic mystical music/qawwali) dissolve ego in divine love.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: What were the core principles of Guru Nanak's spiritual teachings summarized in three cardinal pillars?
options: 1. Nam Japna (Chanting the Name of God) ; 2. Kirt Karna (Honest, ethical labor) ; 3. Vand Chhakna (Sharing one's earnings with others in charity)
explanation: Guru Nanak's core triadic ethics: Nam Japna (devotional remembrance), Kirt Karna (honest labor), and Vand Chhakna (charitable sharing).

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: What was the historical significance of the 'Langar' (community kitchen) instituted by Guru Nanak and expanded by Guru Angad and Guru Amar Das?
options: People of ALL castes, religions, and social backgrounds sat together on the floor (Pangat) to eat the exact same meal together, completely destroying caste taboos and untouchability
It was a restaurant for wealthy merchants
It was a feast held only once a year
Only kings were allowed to eat there
explanation: Langar institutionalized radical social equality: emperor and peasant sat side by side in pangat, sharing identical food prepared communally.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Why did the Mughal Emperor Jahangir view the growing influence and autonomous political-military stature of Guru Arjan Dev Ji as a potential threat, leading to the Guru's martyrdom in 1606?
options: The Sikh community had transformed into a dynamic, prosperous, self-governing socio-religious brotherhood centered at Amritsar, attracting large numbers of both Hindu and Muslim followers
Because Guru Arjan refused to pay road tax
Because the Sikhs built a navy
Because of a boundary dispute over a farm
explanation: Jahangir recorded in Tuzuk that the expanding spiritual authority of Guru Arjan Dev threatened imperial control, prompting state persecution.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Who founded the 'Khalsa Panth' (the community of the pure saint-soldiers) at Anandpur Sahib on Baisakhi Day in 1699, forging the Sikhs into a formidable martial and spiritual brotherhood?
options: Guru Gobind Singh Ji (the 10th Sikh Guru)
explanation: Guru Gobind Singh Ji established the Khalsa in 1699 with the Five Ks (Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kachhera, Kirpan) to defend justice against tyranny.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Which blind poet of Braj composed the monumental devotional anthology 'Sursagar', celebrating the childhood lilas of Lord Krishna in Brajbhasha?
explanation: Surdas (a disciple of Vallabhacharya) composed the Sursagar, Sur Saravali, and Sahitya Lahari celebrating Krishna's Vatsalya and Madhurya rasas.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: What was the 'Ekasarana Dharma' propagated by Sankaradeva in Assam?
options: Devotional surrender to the Supreme Lord Krishna alone, discarding idol worship and complex rituals, and seeking spiritual solace in chanting the Name of God (Nam-Kirtan)
explanation: Sankaradeva's Ekasarana Dharma focused on monotheistic Krishna bhakti centered on congregational chanting in village Namghars.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: What were the 'Nathpanthis, Siddhas, and Yogis' who challenged conventional ritual orthodoxy in northern India?
options: Renouncers from lower artisanal groups who advocated intense meditation on formless reality, breathing exercises (Pranayama), yogasanas, and mind-body purification to attain liberation
explanation: Nathpanthis and Yogis (associated with Gorakhnath) taught Hatha Yoga, breath control, and inner esoteric realization beyond ritual dogma.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Who was the revered 14th-century Sufi saint of Delhi known as 'Mehboob-e-Ilahi' (Beloved of God), who lived in Ghyaspur (Delhi) and inspired Amir Khusrau?
explanation: Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya preached boundless charity and tolerance; his court disciple Amir Khusrau pioneered Hindavi and Qawwali music.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: In what language did Kabir compose his powerful verses (Sakhis, Dohas, and Rekhtas)?
options: In the rough, rustic colloquial vernacular Hindi of the common people (Saddukkadi / Khari Boli / Bhojpuri), making them directly accessible to ordinary peasants and weavers
explanation: Kabir wrote in direct, forceful vernacular Hindi (Saddukkadi), utilizing sharp colloquial idioms that pierced through scholastic pretension.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question:
Read the statements:
Assertion (A): The medieval Bhakti and Sufi movements constituted a profound socio-cultural revolution that democratized spiritual access in India.
Reason (R): Bhakti and Sufi saints composed their hymns in regional vernacular languages (Tamil, Marathi, Awadhi, Brajbhasha, Assamese, Punjabi), discarded the monopoly of Sanskrit and Arabic, rejected caste hierarchies, and opened spiritual salvation to women and lower-caste communities.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: Bhakti-Sufi synthesis was an egalitarian linguistic and social democratization: vernacular poetry shattered elite scriptural monopolies.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question:
Spot the IMPOSTER in the following group of Bhakti Saints and their signature devotional masterworks:
Group:
1. Tulsidas - Ramcharitmanas
2. Surdas - Sursagar
3. Guru Arjan Dev - Compilation of Adi Granth
4. Sant Kabir - The Encyclopedia of 18th-century French Chemistry
options: Masterwork 4 (Sant Kabir composed the BIJAK, Sakhis, and Dohas, NOT French chemistry books)
explanation: Masterwork 4 is an absurd impossibility: Kabir's timeless legacy resides in the Bijak, Kabir Granthavali, and Adi Granth selections.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question:
Analyze the philosophical distinction between 'NIRGUNA BHAKTI' and 'SAGUNA BHAKTI':
How did these two streams conceptualize the divine?
options: Nirguna Bhakti (Kabir, Guru Nanak) envisioned God as the abstract, formless, attribute-less ultimate spiritual Truth ; Saguna Bhakti (Tulsidas, Surdas, Mirabai, Chaitanya) worshipped God in tangible human incarnational forms (Avatars like Rama and Krishna) through personal devotion
Nirguna Bhakti is worship of trees and Saguna Bhakti is worship of fire
Nirguna Bhakti was practiced only by kings
Both are identical without any difference
explanation: Nirguna (formless transcendent monotheism) vs Saguna (immanent anthropomorphic avatar devotion) form the twin philosophical pillars of Bhakti.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question:
Match Column I (Bhakti / Sufi Masters) with Column II (Primary Regional Sphere of Devotion):

(c) Srimanta Sankaradeva   -> (iii) Assam (Brahmaputra Valley / Satras & Namghars)
(d) Khwaja Muinuddin       -> (iv) Rajasthan (Ajmer / Chishti Sufi Silsila)
explanation: Basavanna = Karnataka; Jnaneshwar/Tukaram = Maharashtra; Sankaradeva = Assam; Muinuddin = Ajmer.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question:

Statement 1: The annual Varkari Palkhi pilgrimage to Pandharpur on Ashadhi Ekadashi unites hundreds of thousands of pilgrims singing Abhangas of Dnyaneshwar and Tukaram.
Statement 2: The Marathi Bhakti movement emphasized that the temple of God resides within the compassionate human heart rather than in external ascetic withdrawal.
Statement 3: Sant Tukaram declared that only wealthy Brahmans could enter heaven.
Which statements are TRUE?
explanation: Statement 3 is false (Tukaram fiercely opposed caste elitism and hypocrisy). Statements 1 and 2 represent true Varkari ethos.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Why did Mirabai's fearless rejection of caste and royal Mewar palace luxury make her an enduring symbol of feminist and social defiance in Indian history?
options: She openly defied royal patriarchy, drank poison sent by the Rana without fear, accepted the low-caste leather worker Sant Ravidas as her Guru, and sang in public streets dedicated only to Krishna
She built an army to conquer Delhi
She became the queen of Portugal
explanation: Mirabai dismantled Rajput patriarchal and caste norms: taking Sant Ravidas (a Chamar) as guru and proclaiming autonomous spiritual sovereignty.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: How did the compilation of the 'Guru Granth Sahib' embody an unprecedented inter-faith ecumenical syncretism?
options: It sanctified and bound together the holy compositions of Sikh Gurus alongside the verses of Hindu Bhakti saints (Jaidev, Namdev, Ravidas, Ramananda) and Muslim Sufi mystics (Baba Farid, Kabir, Bhagat Bhikhan) under one supreme eternal Scripture
It was written only in Persian
explanation: The Guru Granth Sahib is an ecumenical masterpiece of interfaith harmony, enshrining Bhagat Bani from 15 diverse Hindu and Muslim saints.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: What was the revolutionary social function of 'Namghars' established by Sankaradeva across Assamese villages?
options: Village community prayer halls that served simultaneously as sacred sanctuaries for chanting, local courts for resolving disputes, community theaters for Ankiya Nat dramas, and village libraries
explanation: Namghars functioned as decentralized socio-cultural epicenters integrating congregational prayer, Assamese Vaishnava drama (Bhaona), and village democracy.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question:
Consider four foundational tenets of the Chishti Sufi order in India:
1. Rejection of worldly wealth and refusal of royal court appointments
2. Open hospitality and langar feeding the hungry without religious distinction
3. Adoption of local Indian vernacular languages (Hindavi) and musical forms
4. Preaching 'Sulh-i Kul' (Universal Peace with all creation)
What made the Chishti saints universally beloved across all communities in India?
options: Their genuine ascetic purity, deep compassion for the impoverished, and cultural synthesis with local Indian traditions
Their strict enforcement of foreign languages
explanation: Chishti masters cultivated profound cross-cultural empathy: living in austere poverty, embracing Hindavi poetry, and championing universal brotherhood.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: Why did Sant Kabir relentlessly lampoon both orthodox Hindu Pandits and Muslim Qazis in his verses?
options: He believed that external ritual dogmas (sacred threads, temple pilgrimages, circumcisions, ritual fasts) were meaningless hypocrisies that divided humanity and blinded people to the divine residing within every human heart
Because Kabir wanted to become a king
Because he wanted to sell books
explanation: Kabir's razor-sharp verses deconstructed scholastic dogmatism: 'Moko kahan dhundhe re bande, main to tere paas mein' (Where do you search for Me? I am beside you).

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: What is the enduring cultural impact of the Bhakti movement on the modern regional languages and literature of India?
options: It gave birth to the golden age of regional Indian vernacular literatures (Tamil, Kannada, Marathi, Hindi, Assamese, Bengali, Punjabi, Gujarati), elevating popular speech into exquisite classical literary idioms
It caused all regional languages to disappear
It forced everyone to speak English
It stopped people from writing poetry
explanation: Bhakti literature was the catalyst for the flowering of modern Indian languages, infusing vernacular poetry with emotional resonance and philosophical depth.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Devotional Paths to the Divine
question: What overarching humanist spiritual vision is celebrated in Chapter 8 of NCERT Class 7 History?
options: The transcendent universal message that the divine is accessed not through rigid caste barriers, empty ritualism, or institutional dogma, but through pure, unconditional love, inner moral righteousness, and compassionate service to all living beings
That only kings can achieve salvation
That rituals are the only way to reach God
That humanity was divided forever without hope
explanation: Chapter 8 illuminates the transformative spiritual ethos of medieval India: love as the supreme path to God and universal compassion as the highest worship.

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: संज्ञा के स्थान पर प्रयुक्त होने वाले सार्थक शब्दों को व्याकरण में क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: सर्वनाम: जो शब्द संज्ञा के स्थान पर भाषा को सुंदर, संक्षिप्त और पुनरुक्ति-दोष से मुक्त बनाने के लिए प्रयुक्त होते हैं, उन्हें सर्वनाम कहते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: हिंदी व्याकरण में सर्वनाम के मुख्य रूप से कितने भेद होते हैं?
options: 6 भेद (पुरुषवाचक, निश्चयवाचक, अनिश्चयवाचक, संबंधवाचक, प्रश्नवाचक, निजवाचक)
explanation: सर्वनाम के 6 भेद होते हैं: 1. पुरुषवाचक, 2. निश्चयवाचक, 3. अनिश्चयवाचक, 4. संबंधवाचक, 5. प्रश्नवाचक, 6. निजवाचक।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: वक्ता (बोलने वाले), श्रोता (सुनने वाले) अथवा किसी अन्य व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयुक्त होने वाले सर्वनाम को क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम वक्ता, श्रोता या अन्य तीसरे व्यक्ति का बोध कराते हैं (इसके 3 भेद होते हैं: उत्तम, मध्यम, अन्य पुरुष)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'मैं, हम, मुझे, मेरा, हमारा' शब्द पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम के किस उप-भेद के अंतर्गत आते हैं?
options: उत्तम पुरुष (First Person - बोलने वाला वक्ता)
explanation: बोलने वाला (वक्ता) अपने लिए जिन सर्वनामों का प्रयोग करता है, वे 'उत्तम पुरुष' कहलाते हैं (जैसे: मैं, हम)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'तू, तुम, आप, तुझे, तुम्हारा' शब्द पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम के किस उप-भेद के अंतर्गत आते हैं?
options: मध्यम पुरुष (Second Person - सुनने वाला श्रोता)
explanation: श्रोता (सुनने वाले) के लिए प्रयुक्त होने वाले सर्वनाम 'मध्यम पुरुष' कहलाते हैं (जैसे: तू, तुम, आप)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'वह, वे, यह, ये, उसे, उनका' शब्द पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम के किस उप-भेद के अंतर्गत आते हैं?
options: अन्य पुरुष (Third Person - जिसके विषय में बात की जाए)
explanation: वक्ता और श्रोता जिसके बारे में बात करते हैं, वे 'अन्य पुरुष' कहलाते हैं (जैसे: वह, वे)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: जो सर्वनाम किसी निश्चित व्यक्ति, वस्तु या घटना की ओर संकेत करते हैं (जैसे: 'यह मेरी पुस्तक है', 'वह मेरा घर है'), उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: निश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम निकट या दूर की निश्चित वस्तु/व्यक्ति का निश्चयपूर्वक बोध कराते हैं (यह, वह, ये, वे)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'दरवाजे पर कोई खड़ा है।' और 'दूध में कुछ गिर गया है।' वाक्यों में 'कोई' और 'कुछ' किस प्रकार के सर्वनाम हैं?
explanation: अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम किसी निश्चित वस्तु या व्यक्ति का बोध नहीं कराते (प्राणियों के लिए 'कोई' तथा पदार्थों के लिए 'कुछ')।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'जो परिश्रम करेगा, वह सफल होगा।' और 'जैसी करनी, वैसी भरनी।' वाक्यों में 'जो-वह', 'जैसी-वैसी' किस प्रकार के सर्वनाम हैं?
explanation: संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम वाक्य में किसी दूसरी संज्ञा या सर्वनाम से संबंध प्रकट करते हैं (जो-सो, जैसा-वैसा, जिसकी-उसकी)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: जिन सर्वनाम शब्दों का प्रयोग किसी व्यक्ति, वस्तु या घटना के विषय में प्रश्न पूछने के लिए किया जाता है (जैसे: 'वहाँ कौन खड़ा है?', 'तुम क्या लाए हो?'), वे क्या कहलाते हैं?
explanation: प्रश्नवाचक सर्वनाम: प्रश्न पूछने के लिए प्रयुक्त होने वाले शब्द (कौन, क्या, किसे, किसको, कहाँ)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'मैं अपना काम स्वयं (खुद / अपने आप) करूँगा।' वाक्य में 'स्वयं' और 'अपने आप' किस प्रकार का सर्वनाम है?
explanation: निजवाचक सर्वनाम: कर्ता अपने लिए जिन शब्दों का प्रयोग करता है (स्वयं, खुद, अपने आप, आप ही)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: हिंदी भाषा में मूल सर्वनाम शब्दों की संख्या कुल कितनी मानी जाती है?
options: 11 मूल सर्वनाम (मैं, तू, आप, यह, वह, जो, सो, कोई, कुछ, कौन, क्या)
explanation: हिंदी व्याकरण में 11 मूल (मौलिक) सर्वनाम माने गए हैं: मैं, तू, आप, यह, वह, जो, सो, कोई, कुछ, कौन, क्या।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: निश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम और सार्वनामिक विशेषण में क्या मुख्य अंतर होता है?
options: जब 'यह' या 'वह' अकेले आकर संज्ञा के स्थान पर प्रयुक्त हों, तो वे 'निश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम' होते हैं (जैसे: 'यह मेरा घर है') ; परन्तु जब वे संज्ञा से ठीक पहले लगकर उसकी विशेषता बताएँ, तो वे 'सार्वनामिक विशेषण' बन जाते हैं (जैसे: 'यह घर मेरा है')
दोनों में कोई अंतर नहीं होता
सार्वनामिक विशेषण केवल पुल्लिंग होते हैं
सर्वनाम कभी वाक्य में प्रयुक्त नहीं हो सकते
explanation: 'यह मेरी पुस्तक है' = निश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम; 'यह पुस्तक मेरी है' = सार्वनामिक विशेषण (संज्ञा से पूर्व प्रयुक्त)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'आप' शब्द का प्रयोग मध्यम पुरुष और निजवाचक सर्वनाम—दोनों में किस प्रकार भिन्न अर्थ में होता है?
options: श्रोता के आदर के लिए प्रयुक्त 'आप' मध्यम पुरुष होता है (जैसे: 'आप कब आए?'); जबकि कर्ता द्वारा अपने लिए प्रयुक्त 'आप' निजवाचक होता है (जैसे: 'मैं यह काम आप ही कर लूँगा')
'आप' केवल बहुवचन में ही आता है
निजवाचक में 'आप' का प्रयोग अशुद्ध है
explanation: आदरार्थक मध्यम पुरुष: 'आप बैठिए'; निजवाचक (स्वयं के अर्थ में): 'वह अपने आप चला जाएगा'।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'जिसकी लाठी, उसकी भैंस।' वाक्य में 'जिसकी' और 'उसकी' सर्वनाम के किस भेद के उदाहरण हैं?
explanation: 'जिसकी... उसकी' परस्पर आश्रित उपवाक्यों में संबंध स्थापित करने वाले संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'पानी में कुछ पड़ा है।' वाक्य में 'कुछ' का प्रयोग किस संदर्भ में हुआ है?
options: निर्जीव वस्तु या पदार्थ के लिए अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम के रूप में
explanation: 'कुछ' का प्रयोग अप्राणिवाचक (निर्जीव/द्रव्य) अनिश्चित वस्तुओं के लिए होता है ('कोई' का सजीव प्राणियों के लिए)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'बाहर कोई आया है।' वाक्य में 'कोई' का प्रयोग किस संदर्भ में हुआ है?
options: सजीव प्राणी (व्यक्ति) के लिए अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम के रूप में
explanation: 'कोई' प्राणिवाचक अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम है (जैसे: कोई आया है, किसी ने बुलाया है)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'तुमने क्या खाया है?' वाक्य में 'क्या' किस प्रकार का सर्वनाम है?
options: प्रश्नवाचक सर्वनाम (वस्तु/पदार्थ के संबंध में प्रश्न पूछने के लिए)
explanation: 'क्या' अप्राणिवाचक प्रश्नवाचक सर्वनाम है ('कौन' प्राणिवाचक प्रश्नवाचक है)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: सर्वनाम शब्दों में किस कारक की विभक्ति का प्रयोग कभी नहीं होता?
options: संबोधन कारक (हे, अरे, भो का प्रयोग सर्वनामों के साथ नहीं होता)
explanation: सर्वनाम शब्दों में केवल 7 कारकों (कर्ता से अधिकरण तक) की ही रूप-रचना होती है; संबोधन कारक सर्वनामों में नहीं होता।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'मैं' (उत्तम पुरुष एकवचन) का करण कारक में एकवचन रूप क्या बनेगा?
explanation: मैं + से (करण कारक) = मुझसे / मेरे द्वारा।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'वह' (अन्य पुरुष एकवचन) का संप्रदान कारक में बहुवचन रूप क्या होगा?
explanation: वह (बहुवचन 'वे') + को/के लिए = उन्हें / उनके लिए / उनको।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: निम्नलिखित वाक्यों में से 'अशुद्ध सर्वनाम प्रयोग' वाला वाक्य चुनिए:
options: 'तेरे को मेरे से क्या काम है?' (अशुद्ध रूप ; शुद्ध होगा: 'तुम्हें मुझसे क्या काम है?')
explanation: हिंदी मानक व्याकरण में 'तेरे को / मेरे को' अमानक और अशुद्ध है; इसके स्थान पर 'तुझे/तुम्हें' और 'मुझसे' का प्रयोग होता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'यह वही बालक है, जिसे कल पुरस्कार मिला था।' वाक्य में 'जिसे' सर्वनाम का कौन-सा रूप है?
explanation: 'जिसे' संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम 'जो' का कर्म कारक एकवचन रूप है (जो + को = जिसे)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'हम कल मुंबई जाएँगे।' वाक्य में रेखांकित सर्वनाम 'हम' किस वचन और पुरुष में है?
explanation: 'हम' उत्तम पुरुष का बहुवचन रूप है (एकवचन 'मैं' होता है)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'उसकी गाय बहुत सीधी है।' वाक्य में 'उसकी' किस कारक का रूप है?
explanation: वह + का/के/की = उसका / उसकी / उसके (संबंध कारक)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'वे सब अपने घर चले गए।' वाक्य में 'अपने' किस सर्वनाम का उदाहरण है?
explanation: 'अपना / अपनी / अपने' निजवाचक सर्वनाम के रूप हैं, जो कर्ता के स्वयं के संबंध का बोध कराते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'कोई तुम्हें बुला रहा है।' वाक्य में 'कोई' और 'तुम्हें' क्रमशः कौन-से सर्वनाम हैं?
explanation: 'कोई' अनिश्चयवाचक है और 'तुम्हें' मध्यम पुरुष (तुम + को) है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'सच्चा मित्र वही है, जो विपत्ति में काम आए।' वाक्य में 'वही-जो' किस सर्वनाम युग्म का बोध कराते हैं?
explanation: 'वही... जो' सह-संबंधी सर्वनाम हैं जो दो उपवाक्यों को परस्पर जोड़ते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question:
कथन और कारण को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़ें:
कथन (A): 'सर्वनाम शब्दों का अपना कोई स्वतंत्र लिंग नहीं होता ; उनका लिंग उनके स्थान पर आने वाली संज्ञा अथवा क्रिया के रूप से निर्धारित होता है।'
कारण (R): 'वह पढ़ता है' में 'वह' पुल्लिंग है तथा 'वह पढ़ती है' में 'वह' स्त्रीलिंग है, क्योंकि सर्वनाम का रूप दोनों लिंगों में समान रहता है।
सही विकल्प चुनें:
options: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
(A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता।
explanation: सर्वनामों में लिंग-भेद रूपगत नहीं होता; उनका लिंग संदर्भ और क्रिया के अन्वय ('पढ़ता है' / 'पढ़ती है') से स्पष्ट होता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question:
Spot the IMPOSTER in the following group of सर्वनाम और उनके भेद वर्गीकरण में:
Group:
1. 'हम' - उत्तम पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम
2. 'कुछ' - अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम
3. 'स्वयं' - निजवाचक सर्वनाम
4. 'सुंदर' - निश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम
options: वर्गीकरण 4 ('सुंदर' सर्वनाम नहीं, बल्कि गुणवाचक विशेषण [Adjective] है)
explanation: 'सुंदर' गुणवाचक विशेषण है, सर्वनाम नहीं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question:
सुमेलित कीजिए (सर्वनाम शब्द और उनका सही भेद):
(क) जो... सो -> (i) संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम
(ख) आप ही    -> (ii) निजवाचक सर्वनाम
(ग) कोई      -> (iii) अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम
(घ) कौन      -> (iv) प्रश्नवाचक सर्वनाम
explanation: जो-सो = संबंधवाचक; आप ही = निजवाचक; कोई = अनिश्चयवाचक; कौन = प्रश्नवाचक।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: निम्नलिखित वाक्यों में से किस वाक्य में 'निजवाचक सर्वनाम' का बिल्कुल शुद्ध प्रयोग हुआ है?
options: 'मैं यह निबंध स्वयं अपने हाथों से लिखूँगा।'
'आप भला तो जग भला' में 'आप' केवल अन्य पुरुष है।
explanation: 'स्वयं' का प्रयोग कर्ता के अपने आत्म-बोध हेतु निजवाचक सर्वनाम के रूप में शुद्ध है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'यह' सर्वनाम के तिर्यक (विभक्ति-सहित) एकवचन और बहुवचन रूप क्रमशः क्या होते हैं?
options: एकवचन: 'इस' (जैसे: इसने, इसको, इससे) ; बहुवचन: 'इन' (जैसे: इन्होंने, इनको, इनसे)
explanation: 'यह' का तिर्यक रूप एकवचन में 'इस' और बहुवचन में 'इन' होता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'वह' सर्वनाम के तिर्यक (विभक्ति-सहित) एकवचन और बहुवचन रूप क्रमशः क्या होते हैं?
options: एकवचन: 'उस' (जैसे: उसने, उसको, उससे) ; बहुवचन: 'उन' (जैसे: उन्होंने, उनको, उनसे)
explanation: 'वह' का तिर्यक रूप एकवचन में 'उस' और बहुवचन में 'उन' होता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: निम्नलिखित वाक्यों में से 'शुद्ध वाक्य' का चयन कीजिए:
options: 'मैंने अपना काम समय पर पूरा कर लिया है।' (शुद्ध निजवाचक अन्वय)
'मैंने मेरा काम समय पर पूरा कर लिया है।'
explanation: कर्ता के स्वयं के संदर्भ में 'मेरा/उसके/हमारा' के स्थान पर 'अपना/अपनी/अपने' का प्रयोग ही व्याकरणिक दृष्टि से शुद्ध होता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: संयुक्त सर्वनाम (Compound Pronouns) जैसे 'कोई-न-कोई', 'कुछ-न-कुछ', 'जो-कोई', 'सब-कुछ' किस प्रकार के सर्वनाम होते हैं?
options: जब दो या दो से अधिक सर्वनाम शब्द मिलकर एक विशिष्ट यौगिक सर्वनाम का निर्माण करते हैं
अव्ययीभाव समास के उदाहरण मात्र होते हैं
explanation: डॉ. दीमशित्स के अनुसार, 'कोई न कोई, कुछ न कुछ, जो कोई, सब कुछ' संयुक्त सर्वनाम कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'गांधीजी राष्ट्रपिता कहलाए। आपने देश को अहिंसा का पाठ पढ़ाया।' इस दूसरे वाक्य में 'आपने' किस पुरुष का बोध करा रहा है?
options: अन्य पुरुष (आदरार्थक ऐतिहासिक महापुरुष के परिचय के संदर्भ में 'आप' का अन्य पुरुष के रूप में प्रयोग)
explanation: किसी अनुपस्थित आदरणीय महापुरुष का परिचय देते समय 'आप' का प्रयोग 'अन्य पुरुष' के रूप में होता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'किस-किस ने अपना गृहकार्य नहीं किया?' वाक्य में 'किस-किस' किस प्रकार का सर्वनाम रूप है?
options: पुनरुक्त प्रश्नवाचक सर्वनाम (विस्तार एवं अनेकता का बोध कराने वाला)
explanation: प्रश्नवाचक सर्वनाम की पुनरुक्ति ('किस-किस', 'क्या-क्या') बहुलता और व्यापकता का बोध कराती है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: 'जो करेगा, सो भरेगा।' वाक्य में 'सो' के स्थान पर आधुनिक मानक हिंदी में किस सर्वनाम का प्रयोग अधिक प्रचलित है?
explanation: प्राचीन हिंदी में 'सो' संबंधवाचक था; आधुनिक मानक हिंदी में 'जो' के सह-संबंधी के रूप में 'वह' प्रयुक्त होता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 8: सर्वनाम और उसके भेद
question: सर्वनाम (Pronoun) के सम्यक ज्ञान और सटीक प्रयोग का भाषा की अभिव्यक्ति में क्या सर्वोच्च महत्व है?
options: सर्वनाम संज्ञा की अवांछित पुनरावृत्ति (Repetition) को रोककर भाषा में संक्षिप्तता, लालित्य, गतिशीलता और तार्किक सुसंबद्धता (Cohesion) स्थापित करते हैं
सर्वनाम केवल काव्य में प्रयुक्त होते हैं
सर्वनाम के बिना भी भाषा पूर्णतः शुद्ध रहती है
सर्वनाम केवल संख्याओं को गिनने के काम आते हैं
explanation: सर्वनाम संज्ञा की नीरस पुनरुक्ति दूर कर गद्य एवं पद्य में प्रवाहमयता, संक्षिप्तता और संरचनात्मक सुदृढ़ता प्रदान करते हैं।
